slides.say: For every number t, diamond of t is equal to t squared. In the choices, x is zero or more. Which of the following is not always true?

Before we start, a small tip. Look at the choices. The diamond appears in every choice, and we have to use it two or three times in each one. That can take time. So in the exam, if a question like this looks long, you can leave it for later. Solve the rest of the section first, and come back to it at the end. Here in the lesson, let's solve it. [short pause] We'll solve it in two different ways, with algebra, and then by plugging in a number.

[short pause] Let's start with the math way. With algebra, we write what the diamond does on each side. The diamond squares whatever goes in. Choice number one. On the left, six x goes in, so we get six x, squared. That's six squared times x squared, thirty-six x squared. On the right, thirty-six times x squared. Both sides are equal for every x, so this one is always true, and it's out.
Choice number two. Diamond of root x is root x, squared, which is x. So the left side is x times x, which is x squared. The right side is diamond of x, x squared too. Always true, so it's out.

Choice number three. On the left, five x, squared, is twenty-five x squared. On the right, five times x squared is only five x squared. These are equal only when x is zero. For any other x, they're different. So this one is not always true, and choice number three is our answer.
at: and choice number three is our answer

slides.say: In the exam you'd circle it and move on. But choice number four teaches something useful. x minus seven and seven minus x are opposites, and opposites have the same square. So the two sides are always equal.

[pause] Now let's plug in a number. It's usually faster, because we don't open anything. Let's take x is one, because it's easy and it's not zero. Zero is allowed too, but zero turns many of these products into zero. Choice number one. Diamond of six is thirty-six, and thirty-six times diamond of one is thirty-six times one, thirty-six. Equal. Choice number two. Diamond of one is one, and one times one is one. Diamond of one is one too. Equal.
at: Diamond of one is one too

slides.say: Choice number three. Diamond of five is twenty-five, but five times diamond of one is five times one, which is five. Twenty-five is not five, so choice number three fails.

One allowed example where a choice fails proves it's not always true, so we can stop here without checking choice number four. Choice number three is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
